patch_description: This approach estimates whether a demand can use a selected two-link route, then rewards that route only when both links are present. It combines those path-completion rewards with direct-link value and a mild congestion penalty for pairs of links that share a heavily loaded endpoint. Demand is normalized using a blend of peak and positive-traffic mean, so a few exceptionally large entries are less likely to suppress the rest of the signal. The resulting sparse, demand-conditioned terms aim to encourage useful relays without making every two-hop path equally attractive.
